Settings

What this is

The MCRNet brings together the Jesus College MCR calendar, your sign-ups, notices, room bookings, Feedback, meetings and minutes, and officer contacts. Access is through your University account. The intranet is private and maintained by the MCR committee. It is not an official Jesus College publication.

Your name

This appears on sign-up lists and next to anything you post. Everything else comes from your University account.

Your entry on the committee

Update the name, role and photograph shown on your committee entry.

Everything the MCR does

Subscribe to all MCR events. The calendar updates automatically and shows every event, whether you have signed up or not.

Only what you are down for

Your personal calendar includes the events you have signed up for. Choose a reminder below. Reminders come from your calendar, rather than by email from the app.

Reset the link if you have shared it by mistake. This creates a new link and disables the old one.

Out of the ordinary

Every time the app refuses to do something it is written down here, with the address the person was signed in as: a member reaching for a committee action, an administrator reaching for something only you can do, a session token that was never issued, a sign in Google would not vouch for, somebody hammering one part of the app. A few things that are allowed are here too, because they are worth being able to account for afterwards: emptying a year of records, exporting the sign up lists, changing who is an administrator.

The address and the CRSid come from the Google sign in and cannot be typed in by hand, so they are the strongest identifier this app has. Nothing in the app can clear this list.

The committee

Who can edit, and who serves what

Administrators

An address on this list is an administrator from the moment they sign in, whether or not they are on the roster below. They see every event, every thread that is not welfare, and can edit any of it. The President's address is on the list permanently.

The roster

Anyone here is recognised as committee when they sign in. Their team decides where they appear on the People page, and a photograph makes a name into a person you can find.

Where notifications go

Notifications go to the address below when a member sends a request that needs attention. Emails say what is waiting, without including confidential messages. Open the intranet to read and respond.

Leave it empty and the app sends nothing at all.

If the emails are not arriving

Mail goes out through the account’s own mailbox, under its own address, with no name laid over the top and a reply-to pointing at whoever made the request. MailApp is not used: it goes by Google’s generic relay and Exchange drops it at the door.

If a notification is missing, check the delivery status above. If it was sent, add the sending address in Outlook under Settings, Mail, Junk email, Safe senders and domains. If there is no delivery record, the app has not sent it.

The button below sends one message by every method there is, with the method written into each subject line. Look at the inbox and at junk, see which numbers arrived, and set How to send to one of them.

If none arrive, check your junk folder and add the sending address in Outlook under Settings, Mail, Junk email, Safe senders and domains.

Who may sign in

By default anyone with a cam.ac.uk address can sign in. Paste CRSids or addresses here, one per line, to limit access to those people.

The programme

One row becomes every week of term, or every second, third or fourth. Cancelling a single week leaves the rest alone.

The MCR’s own formal halls are ordinary one-off events tagged formal, which is all it takes for them to appear under Formals. Add one here, or edit, cancel or delete any of them from the event itself.

Clearing removes the diary and every repeating entry so the committee can add the real one. Approved room bookings are kept. There is no undo.

Feedback on show

Untick a subject and it disappears from Feedback, along with any question asked about it. Nothing is deleted. Tick it again to put it back.

House style

Use these guidelines for notices, event descriptions and replies. You can update them here.

One per line.

Bumps

One row per crew: where they started, and where they finished each of the four days. The chart draws itself, and it appears on Today for the week of the meet and two days after.

Announcements and housekeeping

Forms and links

The addresses the app itself hands out: the room booking form, the maintenance report, the permit, the guest register. Add one, change one, or take one away, and it is on everybody’s page within the minute. Nothing here is in the code any more, so a broken address is a thirty second job rather than a release.

The words on every page

Turn this on and every sentence the app itself writes becomes something you can tap and rewrite, wherever it is: a heading, a button, a note under a card, the small print on the sign in screen. Rewriting one to nothing takes it off the page. Nobody has to touch the code and nothing is lost: the original is always one tap away.

It will not touch anybody's content. Names, event titles, notices, links, and anything a member has written in Feedback or a thread are refused, because rewriting one of those would be the committee editing somebody else's words in everybody's browser. Each of those has its own editor.

What Feedback shows the room

Nothing in Feedback is public until you publish it. Until then a member sees their own answer and no average, no count, no tally, no run of months and none of the words anybody else wrote. Publish a subject or a question one at a time, and take it back the same way.

The Vice-President's address

This list is the only thing that makes somebody a Vice-President as far as this app is concerned, and only the President can write it. It used to recognise anyone whose role on the roster read Vice-President, which meant an administrator could type the words into their own row and be handed the name against every answer in college. Seeing a name is granted here, by one person, or it is not granted. These two seats, and no others, see a name against an answer in Feedback.

One per line.

Taking something away for good

Deleting a formal or an event from its own page announces it: it goes on the board, because a cancellation is news. This does the same job silently. Nothing is written to the board, nobody is told, and there is no undo of any kind. It is for rows that were a mistake, and for clearing out a year that is over.

Wiring for the other MCR apps

The MCRNet
JESUS COLLEGEThe MCRNet

See what’s on at Jesus, book the MCR room, read notices and reach your committee. Sign in with your Cambridge account.

The MCR committee runs this private intranet. It is not an official College publication.

By signing in you agree to the MCR holding your name, your University address and what you put your name down for, under the UK GDPR.

Who holds it. The Jesus College MCR committee, as the data controller. The app runs on the MCR's own Google account and nothing is sold, shared with advertisers, or sent outside it.

What we hold. Your name and your University email address, taken from your Cambridge Google account when you sign in. After that: what you sign up for, what you put on the board, the room bookings you ask for, the threads you open, and how you answer a question in Feedback. Nothing else. We never see or store a password.

Why we may hold it. Because you are a member of the MCR and running the MCR needs it: a list at a door, a room that is not double booked, and an answer that reaches the person who asked. An answer in Feedback is saved with your name against it, and that name is seen by the MCR President and the Vice-President and by nobody else, including the rest of the committee. Where the committee has marked a question as asked without names, no address is saved against your answer at all, only a one way code that cannot be turned back into you.

Who sees it. Other members see your name next to something you put up. The committee sees the running of it. A welfare thread is read by that one officer and the President, and by nobody else, and you may send it without your name at all. In Feedback, the President and the Vice-President see the name against an answer. The rest of the committee reads the same words with no name on them. Who gave which score can be opened by the President alone, and every time it is opened it is written down. A question marked as asked without names is outside all of that: it keeps no address, so there is nothing for anybody to open.

How long. While you are a member, and for the academic year afterwards, after which it is cleared out. A welfare thread is cleared sooner.

Your rights. You may ask to see what is held about you, to have it corrected, or to have it deleted, and you may withdraw from anything you have said yes to. Write to president@mcr.jesus.cam.ac.uk and it will be dealt with within a month. If you are not satisfied you may complain to the Information Commissioner at ico.org.uk.

Use your @cam.ac.uk address. No new password needed.
